```{r, message=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(lubridate)
source("ipm_simulation.R")

# Specify whether to fit the models or load from disk
fit_model = TRUE
```

# Fit all of the CMR data across sites

## Hold cross-site results

```{r}
all_percentages = list()
```

# The data: 22008

```{r}
source("ipm_simulation.R")
site = "22008"

# Load site-level data
fdat = load_field_data(site)
capture = fdat$capture
survey = fdat$survey
initial = fdat$initial

# How many recaptures in different primary periods?
recaptures = capture[, .(primary_period=unique(primary_period)), by=.(pit_tag_id)]
counts = recaptures[, .(count=.N), by=.(pit_tag_id)]
```

## Exploratory data analysis

When were the releases relative to the primary periods?

```{r}
# Plot releases and primary periods
ggplot(survey) + geom_point(aes(x=survey_date, y=primary_period, color=as.factor(primary_period))) +
                 geom_vline(aes(xintercept=unique(capture$release_date)[1])) +
                  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=unique(capture$release_date)[2]))

# What are the release dates?
unique(capture$release_date)

survey[survey_date >= unique(capture$release_date)[1]][, .(secondary_periods=length(secondary_period)) , by=.(primary_period)]

# Last survey
max(survey$survey_date)

primary_periods_dt = survey[, .(mean_survey_date=mean(survey_date)), by=.(primary_period)]
primary_periods_dt$mean_survey_date = as.Date(primary_periods_dt$mean_survey_date)
```

Plot individual trajectories

```{r}

# Drop the captures where no swabs were taken
capture_nona = capture[!is.na(bd_load)]
keep_inds = counts[count >= 1]$pit_tag_id
no_recapture = setdiff(initial$pit_tag_id, capture_nona$pit_tag_id)
no_recap_count = initial[pit_tag_id %in% no_recapture][, .(count=.N), by=.(treatment)][order(treatment)]
all_count = initial[, .(count=.N), by=.(treatment)][order(treatment)]

all_count$percent_no_recapture = no_recap_count$count / all_count$count
all_count$site = site
all_percentages[[site]] = all_count

ggplot(capture_nona[pit_tag_id %in% keep_inds], 
       aes(x=survey_date, y=log(bd_load + 1), color=as.factor(pit_tag_id))) + 
  geom_line() + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~treatment) + 
  #geom_vline(data=survey, aes(xintercept = survey_date), color='gray', alpha=0.2) +
  guides(color = FALSE) + 
  theme_classic() + ylab("log(Bd load + 1)") + xlab("Date")

capture_nona$frog_id = as.integer(as.factor(capture_nona$pit_tag_id))

strip_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(all_count$treatment, " (No recapture = ", round(all_count$percent_no_recapture, 2)*100, "%)"),
  all_count$treatment)

ggplot(capture_nona[pit_tag_id %in% keep_inds], 
       aes(x=survey_date, y=as.factor(frog_id))) + 
  geom_line(linewidth=0.1) + geom_point(aes(color=log10(bd_load + 1), shape=as.factor(release_date)), size=3) + 
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=unique(capture$release_date)[1]), linewidth=0.2, color='red') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=unique(capture$release_date)[2]),  linewidth=0.2, color='red') +
  geom_vline(data=primary_periods_dt, aes(xintercept=mean_survey_date), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.1, color='gray') +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scale="free_y", labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels)) +
  scale_color_viridis_b() +
  labs(color = expression(log[10]*"(Bd intensity + 1)"), shape = "Release date") +
  theme_classic() + ylab("Frog ID") + xlab("Date") + 
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.title=element_text(size=9))

ggsave(paste0("../../../results/", site, "_field_trajectories.pdf"), width=8, height=5)
```

Exploratory comparison of infection intensity among treatments

```{r}
ggplot(capture_nona[bd_load > 0]) + geom_boxplot(aes(x=treatment, y=log(bd_load)))
capture_nona[bd_load > 0][, .(mean_load=mean(log(bd_load))), by=.(treatment)]
```

## Format the data for CMR fitting

```{r}

# Data formatting parameters. Set this up to bin by load so that a continuous model could be fit.
# Note that we are not fitting the continuous load model here, but this is a more general approach. 

scale = 1 # Scale for better fitting. Divide natural scale load by this value before logging.
bins = 50 # Number of load bins
min_size = -6 # Lower bound (depends on scale)
max_size = 20 # Upper bound (depends on scale)
time_step = 7 # Model time step in days

mdat = format_field_data_for_fitting(scale, bins, min_size, max_size, 
                                     time_step, capture, survey, initial, site)
```

Set up the formatted data for the Stan model fitting

```{r}
keep_inds = 1:nrow(mdat$obs_states_noload)
tobs_states = mdat$obs_states[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_obs = mdat$secondary_obs[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_periods = mdat$secondary_periods[keep_inds, ]
tobs_states_noload = mdat$obs_states_noload[keep_inds, ]
texposure = mdat$exposure[keep_inds]
tload_states = mdat$load_states[keep_inds, ]

# Assign cohort information. There are two released cohorts for site 22008
cohort = ifelse(tobs_states[, 1] != -1, 1, 2)
cohort2_ind = which.max(tobs_states[, 1] == -1)
t2 = which(mdat$obs_states[cohort2_ind, ] != -1)[1] # Time step where we can actually observe the second cohort
```

## Set-up the Stan data

```{r}

# Set-up stan data for no load CMR model
standata_noload = list(
      T=ncol(tobs_states_noload),
      N=nrow(tobs_states_noload),
      obs_states = tobs_states_noload,
      secondary_periods=tsecondary_periods,
      secondary_obs=tsecondary_obs,
      load=tload_states,
      num_states=3,
      exposure=texposure,
      cohort=cohort,
      t2=t2
)
```

## Model fitting

Load the Stan models.

```{r}
model_noload = cmdstan_model(stan_file="stanfiles/cmr_field_exposure.stan")
```

Fit the CMR model

```{r}
if(fit_model){
  fit_noload = model_noload$sample(data=standata_noload, iter_warmup=800, 
                                   iter_sampling = 2000, 
                                   chains=4, parallel_chains = 4, 
                                   adapt_delta=0.93)
  saveRDS(fit_noload, file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
} else {
  fit_noload = readRDS(file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
}
```

## Examine model output

Examine fitting diagnostics

```{r}
fit_noload$summary()
```

Check diagnostics

```{r}
draw_df = as_draws_df(fit_noload$draws())
mcmc_trace(draw_df)
mcmc_rank_overlay(draw_df)
```

Here, we are simply drawing from the posteriors and then projecting the transition matricies forward in time
to predict the survival curves for exposed and unexposed frogs.

```{r}
post_draws = as_draws_df(fit_noload$draws())

# Extract params
mparams = as.list(colMeans(post_draws))
rand_draws = 200 # Number of random curves to generate
steps = 162 # Duration of the forward simulation
curves_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))
curves_exp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))

for(i in 1:rand_draws){
  
  j = sample(1:500, 1)
  mparams = post_draws[j, ]
  
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Unexposed
  surv_prob0 = pnorm(mparams$surv_int)
  surv_probinf = average_probit(mparams$surv_int, -1*mparams$surv_slope, 
                                mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  trans_prob = pnorm(mparams$trans_int)
  loss_prob = average_probit(mparams$loss_int, mparams$loss_slope, 
                             mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Exposed
  surv_prob0_e = pnorm(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure)
  surv_probinf_e = average_probit(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure,
                                  -1*mparams$surv_slope, 
                                  mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure,
                                  mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))
  loss_prob_e = average_probit(mparams$loss_int + mparams$loss_int_exposure, 
                               mparams$loss_slope,  
                               mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure,
                               mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))

  Tmat_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_exp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_unexp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1) # If you are dead, stay dead
  Tmat_unexp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0)
  Tmat_unexp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf*(loss_prob), surv_probinf*(1 - loss_prob), 1 - surv_probinf)
  
  Tmat_exp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1)
  Tmat_exp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0_e*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0_e*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0_e)
  Tmat_exp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf_e*(loss_prob_e), surv_probinf_e*(1 - loss_prob_e), 1 - surv_probinf_e)
  
  init = c(1, 0, 0)
  surv_probs = array(NA, dim=steps)
  states = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states_e = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states[, 1] = init
  states_e[, 1] = init
  
  for(t in 1:steps){
    states[, t + 1] = states[, t] %*% Tmat_unexp
    states_e[, t + 1] = states_e[, t] %*% Tmat_exp
  }
  
  curves_unexp[, i] = 1 - states[3, ]
  curves_exp[, i] = 1 - states_e[3, ]

}
```

```{r}
library(reshape2)

# Plot the curves
melt_ce = melt(curves_exp)
melt_cue = melt(curves_unexp)
colnames(melt_ce) = c("time", "sample", "surv_prob")
colnames(melt_cue) = c("time", "sample", "surv_prob")
melt_ce$exposure = "exposed"
melt_cue$exposure = "unexposed"
all_trajs = as.data.table(rbind(melt_ce, melt_cue))
all_trajs_sum = all_trajs[, .(median=median(surv_prob), 
                              lower=quantile(surv_prob, 0.05), 
                              upper=quantile(surv_prob, 0.95)),
                          by=.(exposure, time)]

t_p1 = ggplot() +
           geom_line(data=all_trajs_sum, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, 
                                             y=median, color=exposure), size=2) +
           geom_ribbon(data=all_trajs_sum, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, 
                                               ymin=lower, ymax=upper, 
                                               fill=exposure), alpha=0.5) +
           theme_classic() + xlab("Years") + ylab("Survival probability") + 
           theme(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.9))

t_p1
        
```

```{r}
all_trajs_sum[time == 53]
```

Makes the parameter plots

```{r}
compare_vars = c("surv_int_exposure", "loss_int_exposure", 
                 "mean_load_exposure", "sigma_load_exposure")
compare_draws = fit_noload$draws(variables = compare_vars)
t_p2 = bayesplot::mcmc_areas(compare_draws, prob=0.95) + xlab("Effect size")
t_p2 = t_p2 +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "sigma_load_exposure"     = expression(s[1] * "," ~ "variance effect"),
      "mean_load_exposure" = expression(gamma[1] * "," ~ "intensity effect"),
      "loss_int_exposure"     = expression(alpha[1] * "," ~ "loss effect"),
      "surv_int_exposure"  = expression(beta[1] * "," ~ "survival effect")
    )
  )
t_p2
```

```{r}
library(patchwork)
t_p2 + t_p1
ggsave(paste0("../../../results/", site, "_model_results.pdf"), width=8, height=4)
```

## Format the data for CMR fitting

```{r}
# Data formatting parameters

scale = 1 # Scale for better fitting. Divide natural scale load by this value before logging.
bins = 50 # Number of load bins
min_size = -6 # Lower bound
max_size = 20 # Upper bound
time_step = 7 # Model time step in days

mdat = format_field_data_for_fitting(scale, bins, min_size, max_size, 
                                     time_step, capture, survey, initial, site)
```

```{r}
keep_inds = 1:nrow(mdat$obs_states)
tobs_states = mdat$obs_states[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_obs = mdat$secondary_obs[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_periods = mdat$secondary_periods[keep_inds, ]
tobs_states_noload = mdat$obs_states_noload[keep_inds, ]
texposure = mdat$exposure[keep_inds]
tload_states = mdat$load_states[keep_inds, ]

# This site has two release cohorts
cohort = ifelse(tobs_states[, 1] != -1, 1, 2)
cohort2_ind = which.max(tobs_states[, 1] == -1)
t2 = which(mdat$obs_states[cohort2_ind, ] != -1)[1]
```

## Set-up the Stan data

```{r}
# Set-up stan data for no load CMR model
standata_noload = list(
      T=ncol(tobs_states_noload),
      N=nrow(tobs_states_noload),
      obs_states = tobs_states_noload,
      secondary_periods=tsecondary_periods,
      secondary_obs=tsecondary_obs,
      load=tload_states,
      num_states=3,
      exposure=texposure,
      cohort=cohort,
      t2=t2
)
```

## Model fitting

```{r}
model_noload = cmdstan_model(stan_file="stanfiles/cmr_field_exposure.stan")
```

Fit the no load CMR model

```{r}
if(fit_model){
  fit_noload = model_noload$sample(data=standata_noload, iter_warmup=500, 
                                   iter_sampling = 1500, 
                                   chains=4, parallel_chains = 4)
  saveRDS(fit_noload, file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
} else {
  fit_noload = readRDS(file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
}
```

Examine the model-predicted survival curve

```{r}
post_draws = as_draws_df(fit_noload$draws())

# Extract params
mparams = as.list(colMeans(post_draws))
rand_draws = 200
steps = 162
curves_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))
curves_exp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))

for(i in 1:rand_draws){
  
  j = sample(1:500, 1)
  mparams = post_draws[j, ]
  
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Unexposed
  surv_prob0 = pnorm(mparams$surv_int)
  surv_probinf = average_probit(mparams$surv_int, -1*mparams$surv_slope, 
                                mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  trans_prob = pnorm(mparams$trans_int)
  loss_prob = average_probit(mparams$loss_int, mparams$loss_slope, 
                             mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Exposed
  surv_prob0_e = pnorm(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure)
  surv_probinf_e = average_probit(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure,
                                  -1*mparams$surv_slope, 
                                  mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure,
                                  mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))
  loss_prob_e = average_probit(mparams$loss_int + mparams$loss_int_exposure, 
                               mparams$loss_slope,  
                               mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure,
                               mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))
  # Build the transition matrix
  Tmat_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_exp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_unexp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1)
  Tmat_unexp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0)
  Tmat_unexp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf*(loss_prob), surv_probinf*(1 - loss_prob), 1 - surv_probinf)
  
  Tmat_exp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1)
  Tmat_exp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0_e*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0_e*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0_e)
  Tmat_exp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf_e*(loss_prob_e), surv_probinf_e*(1 - loss_prob_e), 1 - surv_probinf_e)
  
  init = c(1, 0, 0)
  surv_probs = array(NA, dim=steps)
  states = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states_e = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states[, 1] = init
  states_e[, 1] = init
  
  for(t in 1:steps){
    states[, t + 1] = states[, t] %*% Tmat_unexp
    states_e[, t + 1] = states_e[, t] %*% Tmat_exp
  }
  
  curves_unexp[, i] = 1 - states[3, ]
  curves_exp[, i] = 1 - states_e[3, ]

}
```

# The data: 50785

```{r}
source("ipm_simulation.R")
site = "50785"

fdat = load_field_data(site)
capture = fdat$capture
```

### Format the data for CMR fitting

```{r}
source("ipm_simulation.R")

# Data formatting parameters

scale = 1 # Scale for better fitting. Divide natural scale load by this value before logging.
bins = 50 # Number of load bins
min_size = -6 # Lower bound
max_size = 20 # Upper bound
time_step = 7 # Model time step in days

mdat = format_field_data_for_fitting(scale, bins, min_size, max_size, time_step, capture, survey, initial, site)
```

```{r}
dim(mdat$obs_states)
```

```{r}
keep_inds = 1:nrow(mdat$obs_states)
tobs_states = mdat$obs_states[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_obs = mdat$secondary_obs[keep_inds, ]
tsecondary_periods = mdat$secondary_periods[keep_inds, ]
tobs_states_noload = mdat$obs_states_noload[keep_inds, ]
texposure = mdat$exposure[keep_inds]
tload_states = mdat$load_states[keep_inds, ]

# Cohort. Only one cohort released in this site
cohort = ifelse(tobs_states[, 1] != -1, 1, 2)
t2 = max(keep_inds) + 1
```

### Set-up the Stan data

```{r}
# Set-up stan data for no load CMR model
standata_noload = list(
      T=ncol(tobs_states_noload),
      N=nrow(tobs_states_noload),
      obs_states = tobs_states_noload,
      secondary_periods=tsecondary_periods,
      secondary_obs=tsecondary_obs,
      load=tload_states,
      num_states=3,
      exposure=texposure,
      cohort=cohort,
      t2=t2
)
```

### Model fitting

For this site, we assume there is no loss of infection as there is no information to estimate this parameter.

```{r}
model_noload = cmdstan_model(stan_file="stanfiles/cmr_field_exposure_fixedloss.stan")
```

```{r}
fit_model = TRUE
if(fit_model){
  fit_noload = model_noload$sample(data=standata_noload, iter_warmup=800, 
                                   iter_sampling = 2000, chains=4, 
                                   parallel_chains = 4)
  saveRDS(fit_noload, file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
} else {
  fit_noload = readRDS(file.path("..", "..", "..", "results", paste0(site, "_mcmc", ".rds")))
}
```

## Examine model output

Examine fitting diagnostics

```{r}
fit_noload$summary()
```

```{r}
draw_df = as_draws_df(fit_noload$draws())
mcmc_trace(draw_df)
```

Examine the model-predicted survival curve

```{r}
post_draws = as_draws_df(fit_noload$draws())

# Extract params
mparams = as.list(colMeans(post_draws))
rand_draws = 200
steps = 162
curves_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))
curves_exp = array(NA, dim=c(steps + 1, rand_draws))

for(i in 1:rand_draws){
  
  j = sample(1:500, 1)
  mparams = post_draws[j, ]
  #mparams = as.list(colMeans(post_draws))
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Unexposed
  surv_prob0 = pnorm(mparams$surv_int)
  surv_probinf = average_probit(mparams$surv_int, -1*mparams$surv_slope, mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  trans_prob = pnorm(mparams$trans_int)
  loss_prob = 0 #average_probit(mparams$loss_int, mparams$loss_slope, mparams$mean_load, mparams$sigma_load)
  
  # Set-up transition matrix parameters: Exposed
  surv_prob0_e = pnorm(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure)
  surv_probinf_e = average_probit(mparams$surv_int + mparams$surv_int_exposure, -1*mparams$surv_slope, mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure, mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))
  loss_prob_e = 0 #average_probit(mparams$loss_int + mparams$loss_int_exposure, mparams$loss_slope,  mparams$mean_load + mparams$mean_load_exposure, mparams$sigma_load*exp(mparams$sigma_load_exposure))

  Tmat_unexp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_exp = array(NA, dim=c(3, 3))
  Tmat_unexp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1)
  Tmat_unexp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0)
  Tmat_unexp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf*(loss_prob), surv_probinf*(1 - loss_prob), 1 - surv_probinf)
  
  Tmat_exp[3, ] = c(0, 0, 1)
  Tmat_exp[1, ] = c(surv_prob0_e*(1 - trans_prob), surv_prob0_e*trans_prob, 1 - surv_prob0_e)
  Tmat_exp[2, ] = c(surv_probinf_e*(loss_prob_e), surv_probinf_e*(1 - loss_prob_e), 1 - surv_probinf_e)
  
  init = c(1, 0, 0)
  surv_probs = array(NA, dim=steps)
  states = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states_e = array(NA, dim=c(3, steps + 1))
  states[, 1] = init
  states_e[, 1] = init
  
  for(t in 1:steps){
    states[, t + 1] = states[, t] %*% Tmat_unexp
    states_e[, t + 1] = states_e[, t] %*% Tmat_exp
  }
  
  curves_unexp[, i] = 1 - states[3, ]
  curves_exp[, i] = 1 - states_e[3, ]

}
```

```{r}
library(reshape2)

# Plot the curves
melt_ce = melt(curves_exp)
melt_cue = melt(curves_unexp)
colnames(melt_ce) = c("time", "sample", "surv_prob")
colnames(melt_cue) = c("time", "sample", "surv_prob")
melt_ce$exposure = "exposed"
melt_cue$exposure = "unexposed"
all_trajs = as.data.table(rbind(melt_ce, melt_cue))
all_trajs_sum = all_trajs[, .(median=median(surv_prob), lower=quantile(surv_prob, 0.05), upper=quantile(surv_prob, 0.95)),by=.(exposure, time)]

rb_p1 = ggplot() + #geom_line(data=melt_ce, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, y=surv_prob, group=sample, color="exposed"), alpha=0.01) +
           #geom_line(data=melt_cue, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, y=surv_prob, group=sample, color="unexposed"), alpha=0.01) +
           geom_line(data=all_trajs_sum, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, y=median, color=exposure), size=2) +
           geom_ribbon(data=all_trajs_sum, aes(x=(time - 1)*time_step / 365, ymin=lower, ymax=upper, fill=exposure), alpha=0.5) +
           theme_classic() + xlab("Years") + ylab("Survival probability") + theme(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.9))
rb_p1         
```

```{r}
all_trajs_sum$year = ((all_trajs_sum$time -1)*time_step) / 365
all_trajs_sum[time == 53]
```

```{r}
rb_p2 = rb_p2 + 
    scale_y_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "sigma_load_exposure"     = expression(s[1] * "," ~ "variance effect"),
      "mean_load_exposure" = expression(gamma[1] * "," ~ "intensity effect"),
      #"loss_int_exposure"     = expression(alpha[1] * "," ~ "loss effect"),
      "surv_int_exposure"  = expression(beta[1] * "," ~ "survival effect")
    )
  )
rb_p2
```

```{r}
## Data formatting parameters
```

Identify the cohorts

```{r}
keep_inds = 1:nrow(mdat$obs_states)
```
